title.narrative: Provision of Quality, Accessible, Community-Based Essential MHPSS and SRH Services in Gaza

description.narrative: ltpgtThe impact of the war has pushed development in Gaza back by an estimated 69 years, while the health system is collapsing, with only 200 out of 600 health facilities still functional. Preventive and routine services, including sexual and reproductive health (SRH) care, have been severely disrupted. At the same time, prolonged exposure to violence, loss, displacement, and uncertainty has led to a sharp rise in mental health needs and psychosocial distress. According to WHO, more than one million people in Gaza now require Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS). This distress directly affects maternal wellbeing, coping capacity, and access to SRH services, highlighting the need for an integrated response.ltbrgtIn response to these urgent and interconnected needs, the proposed six-month project aims to ensure delivery of accessible, quality MHPSS and SRH services to crisis-affected communities in Gaza, increasing the availability of services, meeting essential needs, and alleviating the burden on overstretched health staff. The project prioritizes the hardest-hit groups, including women and girls, pregnant women, children and adolescents, persons with disabilities, caregivers under severe stress, and other individuals at heightened risk.ltbrgtMdM-CH will deliver community-based MHPSS services through mobile teams, providing individual, group, and family counselling in safe, accessible spaces within shelters. Services will follow MdM-CH standard operating procedures and evidence-based approaches adapted to the emergency context, with a strong focus on reducing psychological distress, strengthening coping mechanisms, and improving daily functioning. MHPSS awareness and psychoeducation sessions will be conducted to reduce stigma, promote help-seeking behaviour, and serve as entry points for identifying individuals requiring further support.ltbrgtMDM-CH will implement the project jointly with the Culture and Free Thought Association (CFTA) to deliver a comprehensive SRH service package through medical points and mobile teams. SRH services will align with the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) and include maternal health care, family planning, SRH awareness, and referral for the clinical management of sexual violence and other specialized services. This integrated approach reduces access barriers, increases service uptake, and ensures dignified, timely care wherever people are displaced.ltbrgtThe project will reinforce referral and coordination mechanisms, ensuring safe, timely, and accountable pathways for individuals requiring specialized MHPSS, SRH, Gender Based Violence (GBV), child protection, or protection services. Service mapping, coordination with clusters and partners, and internal referrals between MdM-CH and CFTA activities will strengthen continuity of care and avoid duplication.ltbrgtMonitoring and evaluation will focus on service accessibility, coverage, quality, and referral effectiveness, using routine service data, standardized tools, and regular supervision to ensure accountability within the six-month timeframe.ltbrgtBy the end of the project, 19,310 Women, Girls, Men and Boys will have improved access to integrated, lifesaving MHPSS and SRH services, strengthened referral pathways, and enhanced coping capacity, contributing to reduced suffering, improved wellbeing, and strengthened community resilience in an ongoing humanitarian crisis.ltbrgtlt/pgt
